en:Excuse me: Excuse me: Use before interrupting or asking for attention; it is not normally thanks.
en:Sorry to interrupt: Sorry to interrupt: Acknowledges an interruption, not an unrelated mistake earlier in the day.
en:May I ask a question?: May I ask a question?: Asks permission to speak; it does not itself state your question.
en:Could I get past, please?: Could I get past, please?: Past here means moving beyond someone, not a past time.
en:Could you repeat that?: Could you repeat that?: Requests repetition of words, not necessarily an explanation of their meaning.
en:Could you speak more slowly?: Could you speak more slowly?: Requests slower speech, not lower volume.
en:How do you spell that?: How do you spell that?: Asks for letters; use a pronunciation question if you need the sound.
en:What does that mean?: What does that mean?: Requests meaning; it does not ask the person to spell the word.
en:need a hand: need a hand: A hand means practical help here, not a literal body part.
en:need to leave: need to leave: Put to before leave; do not use need leaving for this personal necessity.
en:would like to: would like to: Follow with a base verb; would like is a polite desire, not an obligation.
en:have to: have to: Follow with a base verb; in the past use had to, not have to went.
en:in the morning: in the morning: Use in for this general time period, not on the morning without a named day.
en:in the evening: in the evening: Use in the evening; at night refers to a different, sometimes overlapping period.
en:at noon: at noon: Noon means twelve in the daytime; use at, not in noon.
en:on Friday morning: on Friday morning: A named day changes the preposition to on, even before morning.
en:How about taking a break?: How about taking a break?: After about, taking is an -ing form; do not say How about take a break?
en:Why don't we try another route?: Why don't we try another route?: This normally proposes a shared action; it is not asking why the listener refuses.
en:Let's check first: Let's check first: Let's includes the speaker; do not add to before check.
en:We could take the bus: We could take the bus: Could offers an option here; it is not an order or a statement of past ability.
en:Of course: Of course: Accepts or reassures; an impatient tone can make it sound dismissive.
en:I'd be happy to: I'd be happy to: Follow to with a base verb; it expresses willingness, not only happiness.
en:I'm afraid I can't: I'm afraid I can't: Afraid softens a refusal here; it need not describe actual fear.
en:No, not at all: No, not at all: After Do you mind?, no means no objection; it is not refusing permission.
en:once in a while: once in a while: Means occasionally, not once every fixed week or month.
en:every now and then: every now and then: Means occasionally; it does not mean every time.
en:hardly ever: hardly ever: Already has a negative meaning; do not normally add not.
en:twice a week: twice a week: Use twice a week, not two time a week.
en:turn out well: turn out well: Describes the eventual result; change turn to turned for a past event.
en:work out: work out: Can mean succeed or find a solution here; in other contexts it means exercise.
en:in the end: in the end: Means eventually; at the end usually identifies a final point or position.
en:end up doing: end up doing: Follow end up with -ing, not a bare infinitive or to-infinitive.
en:in other words: in other words: Rephrases a point; it should not introduce an unrelated new argument.
en:what I mean is: what I mean is: Clarifies intended meaning; it does not automatically retract the earlier statement.
en:to put it simply: to put it simply: Signals simplification; take care not to sound as though you are belittling the listener.
en:that is to say: that is to say: Introduces a clarification; it is generally more formal than I mean.
en:instead of: instead of: Follow with a noun or -ing; avoid instead of to do in this pattern.
en:rather than: rather than: Keep the alternatives structurally parallel when comparing actions.
en:as an alternative: as an alternative: Actually supply a different option; repeating the original proposal is not an alternative.
en:otherwise: otherwise: Often introduces what happens if the preceding condition is not met.
en:give someone a hand: give someone a hand: This is an offer of practical assistance, not a literal gift of a hand.
en:help out: help out: Often describes practical or temporary assistance; out is part of this phrasal verb.
en:do someone a favour: do someone a favour: Use do a favour, not make a favour.
en:lend a hand: lend a hand: Hand means help; in the past use lent a hand, not lended.
en:it dawned on me: it dawned on me: Follow on with the person who realises something: it dawned on me.
en:figure out: figure out: With a pronoun say figure it out, not figure out it.
en:make sense: make sense: No article is used in make sense; do not say make a sense.
en:put two and two together: put two and two together: Means infer a connection, not literally perform arithmetic in this context.
en:weigh up the options: weigh up the options: Both weigh up the options and weigh the options are valid; up is especially common in British English.
en:take into account: take into account: Keep into account together; taking something into account does not mean accepting it as proven.
en:on the one hand / on the other hand: on the one hand / on the other hand: Use for genuinely contrasting sides, not two versions of the same point.
en:a trade-off: a trade-off: Name the benefit and the cost; a trade-off is not simply any problem.
en:put into practice: put into practice: Means implement an idea; put is also the past form, not putted.
en:follow through on: follow through on: Keep on before the commitment: follow through on a promise.
en:roll out: roll out: Means introduce a service gradually or publicly here; it need not involve literal rolling.
en:get underway: get underway: Means begin or become active; do not confuse underway with being physically underwater.
en:under pressure: under pressure: Describes demands on someone, not successful control of a situation.
en:keep up with: keep up with: Keep with before the thing whose pace you are matching; keeping up is not necessarily understanding everything.
en:spread too thin: spread too thin: Means effort or resources are divided too widely; it is not a comment on body size.
en:take on too much: take on too much: Means accept too much responsibility; take over means assume control from someone else.
en:keep at it: keep at it: Keep at it means persist; keep it means retain an object.
en:stick with it: stick with it: Means continue despite difficulty; it is informal encouragement, not literal sticking.
en:bounce back: bounce back: Means recover after difficulty; it does not mean the setback never occurred.
en:learn from a setback: learn from a setback: Identify what the experience taught you; learning from a setback does not make the setback a success.
en:consistent with: consistent with: Compatibility does not establish that this is the only possible explanation.
en:lend support to: lend support to: Means support, not prove conclusively; keep to before the claim.
en:fall short of establishing: fall short of establishing: Of is followed by -ing here; the evidence fails to establish the conclusion, not necessarily to support it at all.
en:rule out: rule out: Cannot rule out means still possible; it does not mean confirmed.
en:subject to: subject to: States a condition or dependency; it does not mean the condition has already been fulfilled.
en:provided that: provided that: Introduces a required condition; it is not simply adding background information.
en:with the proviso that: with the proviso that: The clause states a limitation on agreement; do not treat support as unconditional.
en:without prejudice to: without prejudice to: Has a specific formal reservation-of-rights meaning; do not use it merely to mean without personal bias.
en:leave something to be desired: leave something to be desired: Conventional understatement for something unsatisfactory; it is not praise of great desirability.
en:room for improvement: room for improvement: Acknowledges a need to improve; it does not necessarily mean total failure.
en:not entirely convincing: not entirely convincing: Expresses a reservation; not entirely convincing does not mean entirely false.
en:a little ambitious: a little ambitious: Can politely question feasibility; context determines whether it is praise or criticism.
en:get the ball rolling: get the ball rolling: Means start a process, not physically kick a ball in this context.
en:kick off: kick off: Means begin an event here; in other contexts it can mean a disturbance.
en:initiate discussions: initiate discussions: Means begin substantive discussion, not necessarily reach agreement.
en:lay the groundwork: lay the groundwork: Means prepare the foundation for later work; it does not claim that the main outcome is already complete.
pt:com licença: com licença: Use before interrupting or moving past someone; it is not a thank-you.
pt:desculpe incomodar: desculpe incomodar: Acknowledges a possible disturbance; it does not imply a serious offence.
pt:posso passar?: posso passar?: Asks for space to pass, not permission to spend time somewhere.
pt:posso fazer uma pergunta?: posso fazer uma pergunta?: Use fazer uma pergunta, not perguntar uma pergunta in this pattern.
pt:pode repetir?: pode repetir?: Requests repetition; name the part you did not hear when useful.
pt:mais devagar: mais devagar: Asks for slower speech, not a quieter voice.
pt:como se escreve?: como se escreve?: Asks for spelling or writing; it does not ask how to pronounce the word.
pt:o que significa?: o que significa?: Asks for meaning, not a repetition of the sound.
pt:precisar de ajuda: precisar de ajuda: Use de before the noun ajuda; do not omit it in this pattern.
pt:precisar sair: precisar sair: The verb follows precisar directly: preciso sair, not preciso de sair in the Brazilian pattern taught here.
pt:ter que: ter que: Follow que with an infinitive; the subject determines the form of ter.
pt:gostaria de: gostaria de: Keep de before the desired noun or infinitive; it expresses a polite wish, not an obligation.
pt:de manhã: de manhã: Names the morning period; de manhã is not a fixed clock time.
pt:à tarde: à tarde: Keep the grave accent in à tarde; this phrase means in the afternoon.
pt:à noite: à noite: Keep the grave accent in à noite; the precise evening/night boundary depends on context.
pt:ao meio-dia: ao meio-dia: Means at twelve in the daytime, not midnight; preserve the hyphen in meio-dia.
pt:que tal...?: que tal...?: In the suggestion taught here, use an infinitive after que tal, not a conjugated personal verb.
pt:por que não...?: por que não...?: Offers an option here; it need not demand a literal explanation of why not.
pt:podíamos: podíamos: This imperfect form can soften a present suggestion; it does not always refer to a past habit.
pt:vamos...?: vamos...?: Includes the speaker in the suggested activity; it is not a command aimed only at the listener.
pt:pois não: pois não: Despite containing não, this service expression can mean certainly or how can I help, not refusal.
pt:claro: claro: Signals agreement here; tone and context can still affect politeness.
pt:sem problema: sem problema: Reassures or grants permission; it does not promise that every possible request is acceptable.
pt:infelizmente, não posso: infelizmente, não posso: Makes refusal clear; infelizmente softens the message without changing the negative meaning.
pt:de vez em quando: de vez em quando: Means occasionally, not at a fixed interval.
pt:às vezes: às vezes: Means sometimes, not every time; preserve the grave accent in às.
pt:quase nunca: quase nunca: Means almost never; in this pattern it already expresses very low frequency.
pt:duas vezes por semana: duas vezes por semana: Use plural vezes after duas, and por before the frequency period.
pt:dar certo: dar certo: Means succeed or work as intended; the past is deu certo, not deu certeza.
pt:dar errado: dar errado: Means go wrong; it does not necessarily say who was responsible.
pt:no fim das contas: no fim das contas: Summarises the eventual outcome; it is not necessarily about financial accounts.
pt:acabar + gerund: acabar + gerund: Acabar followed by a gerund means end up doing; acabar de followed by an infinitive means have just done.
pt:ou seja: ou seja: Restates a point; it should not introduce a contradictory claim without explanation.
pt:isto é: isto é: Introduces clarification, not an additional unrelated example.
pt:em outras palavras: em outras palavras: Reformulates meaning; it does not require translating into another language.
pt:o que quero dizer é que: o que quero dizer é que: Keep que before the explanatory clause; this phrase clarifies what you intend to say.
pt:em vez de: em vez de: Keep de before a noun or infinitive; do not treat em vez as a complete verb phrase.
pt:como alternativa: como alternativa: Introduce a genuinely different option, not just repeat the same proposal.
pt:caso contrário: caso contrário: States what happens otherwise; do not interpret it as confirmation of the earlier condition.
pt:ou então: ou então: Offers a conversational alternative; então is not necessarily a time reference here.
pt:dar uma mão: dar uma mão: Means help; it does not literally involve handing over a body part.
pt:fazer um favor: fazer um favor: Use fazer um favor, not dar um favor in this expression.
pt:ajudar com: ajudar com: Com introduces the task or object; ajudar alguém and ajudar com algo have different structures.
pt:quebrar um galho: quebrar um galho: Means help solve a practical difficulty temporarily, not literally break a branch in this context.
pt:cair a ficha: cair a ficha: Means the realisation finally arrives; it is an informal Brazilian idiom, not a physical falling object here.
pt:se dar conta de: se dar conta de: Keep de before the fact: dar-se conta de que; do not confuse it with dar conta de uma tarefa.
pt:fazer sentido: fazer sentido: Use fazer sentido without an article before sentido.
pt:entender o motivo: entender o motivo: Means understand the reason; it does not necessarily imply agreeing with that reason.
pt:pesar os prós e os contras: pesar os prós e os contras: Compare advantages and disadvantages; do not list only one side as if it settles the decision.
pt:levar em conta: levar em conta: Means consider a factor; taking it into account does not mean treating it as proven.
pt:por um lado / por outro lado: por um lado / por outro lado: Use for contrasting aspects, not identical points stated twice.
pt:abrir mão de: abrir mão de: Means give up or forgo something; retain de before that thing.
pt:pôr em prática: pôr em prática: Means implement a plan; the past forms of pôr are irregular, such as pus and pusemos.
pt:colocar em ação: colocar em ação: Means move into execution, not merely discuss a possible action.
pt:dar andamento a: dar andamento a: Keep a before the process; a plus o becomes ao, as in dar andamento ao projeto.
pt:levar adiante: levar adiante: Means carry a plan forward; it does not necessarily mean the plan is already finished.
pt:dar conta de: dar conta de: Means manage a workload; dar-se conta de means realise a fact and has a different meaning.
pt:ficar sobrecarregado: ficar sobrecarregado: The adjective describes the person or group and must agree: sobrecarregada, sobrecarregados.
pt:assumir responsabilidades: assumir responsabilidades: Means take on duties; the context must show whether those duties were actually completed.
pt:trabalhar sob pressão: trabalhar sob pressão: Use sob pressão for under pressure, not sobre pressão.
pt:não jogar a toalha: não jogar a toalha: Means do not give up; it is an informal boxing metaphor, not a literal instruction about a towel.
pt:seguir em frente: seguir em frente: Means move forward after a difficulty; it does not deny that the difficulty occurred.
pt:dar a volta por cima: dar a volta por cima: Means recover or overcome adversity, not avoid every setback from the start.
pt:persistir no objetivo: persistir no objetivo: Keep the appropriate preposition: persistir no objetivo, not persistir o objetivo.
pt:ser compatível com: ser compatível com: Being compatible with an explanation does not exclude competing explanations.
pt:corroborar: corroborar: Means provide support or confirmation; it need not establish exclusive causation.
pt:não permite concluir: não permite concluir: Limits the conclusion that can be drawn; it does not necessarily say the observation is false.
pt:não descarta: não descarta: Means a possibility has not been excluded; it is not confirmation that it is true.
pt:estar condicionado a: estar condicionado a: A condition is required; condicionado agrees with its subject, and a plus a becomes à.
pt:desde que: desde que: In the conditional sense taught here, use the subjunctive; desde que can also have a temporal meaning elsewhere.
pt:com a ressalva de que: com a ressalva de que: Introduces an explicit reservation; support remains subject to that limitation.
pt:sujeito a: sujeito a: Sujeito agrees with the noun; a indicates what the outcome depends on.
pt:deixar a desejar: deixar a desejar: A conventional restrained criticism meaning fall short of expectations, not literal desire.
pt:haver margem para melhoria: haver margem para melhoria: Points to scope for improvement; it is not automatically a judgment of complete failure.
pt:não ser de todo convincente: não ser de todo convincente: Expresses limited conviction rather than necessarily rejecting every point.
pt:merecer revisão: merecer revisão: Recommends reconsideration; it does not announce that a revised decision has already been made.
pt:dar o pontapé inicial: dar o pontapé inicial: Means initiate something; the metaphor is conversational rather than a literal sporting instruction here.
pt:iniciar os trabalhos: iniciar os trabalhos: Formal wording for starting proceedings; it does not mean hiring workers.
pt:abrir a discussão: abrir a discussão: Means open the discussion; it does not itself settle the issue.
pt:lançar as bases: lançar as bases: Means establish a foundation for later work; the final outcome may still be incomplete.
ja:すみません: すみません: Can attract attention or apologise; this example uses it before a question, not as thanks.
ja:失礼します: 失礼します: Acknowledges entering, leaving or interrupting; it is not a substitute for every kind of apology.
ja:ちょっといいですか: ちょっといいですか: Asks whether the person has a moment; ちょっと does not guarantee a literal very short duration.
ja:通ってもいいですか: 通ってもいいですか: Asks permission to pass through; 通る is movement through a space, not spending time there.
ja:もう一度お願いします: もう一度お願いします: Requests repetition; it does not itself ask for an explanation of meaning.
ja:ゆっくり話してください: ゆっくり話してください: Requests slower speech, not lower volume.
ja:どう書きますか: どう書きますか: Asks how to write the word or characters; pronunciation needs a different question.
ja:どういう意味ですか: どういう意味ですか: Asks for meaning rather than spelling or repetition.
ja:〜たいです: 〜たいです: Attach たい to the verb stem, as in 行きたい; do not attach it to the dictionary form 行く.
ja:〜がほしいです: 〜がほしいです: Use a desired noun before が; do not attach ほしい directly to a dictionary-form verb.
ja:〜たいんですが: 〜たいんですが: An unfinished-sounding clause invites assistance; it need not express a contradiction despite が.
ja:〜たくないです: 〜たくないです: たい changes like an い-adjective: 行きたくない, not 行きたいない.
ja:毎朝（まいあさ）: 毎朝（まいあさ）: 毎朝 normally needs no time particle に; 毎朝に is not the routine pattern taught here.
ja:今夜（こんや）: 今夜（こんや）: 今夜 is relative to now and normally takes no time particle に.
ja:午前中（ごぜんちゅう）: 午前中（ごぜんちゅう）: 午前中 refers to the period before noon; に can mark an event within that period.
ja:週末（しゅうまつ）: 週末（しゅうまつ）: 週末 is a period, not a single fixed clock time; は makes it the topic in this example.
ja:〜ましょう: 〜ましょう: Attach ましょう to the verb stem; it normally proposes an action including the speaker.
ja:〜ませんか: 〜ませんか: The negative question form can invite someone; it does not simply deny that the action occurs.
ja:〜のはどうですか: 〜のはどうですか: Use dictionary-form verb plus の before はどうですか to propose an action.
ja:〜たらどうですか: 〜たらどうですか: Can sound like advice or criticism depending on tone; it is not always a neutral invitation.
ja:はい、お願いします: はい、お願いします: Clearly accepts an offered service; お願いします is not refusing the offer.
ja:もちろんです: もちろんです: Signals willing acceptance; avoid an impatient tone that makes the answer sound obvious.
ja:いいえ、結構です: いいえ、結構です: The explicit いいえ makes this a refusal; 結構です alone can be ambiguous.
ja:すみません、今は難しいです: すみません、今は難しいです: 難しい can politely indicate inability here, not merely that a task is intellectually difficult.
ja:いつも: いつも: Means usually or always in context; do not treat it as a precise percentage in every utterance.
ja:ときどき: ときどき: Means occasionally, not every day or on a fixed weekly schedule.
ja:あまり〜ない: あまり〜ない: Normally pair あまり with a negative predicate for not very often or not very much.
ja:週に二回: 週に二回: に marks the frequency period; the phrase means twice per week, not two weeks.
ja:うまくいく: うまくいく: Means work out successfully; the past is うまくいった, not うまくいくた.
ja:失敗する: 失敗する: Names an unsuccessful action or result; it does not automatically blame a particular person.
ja:結局（けっきょく）: 結局（けっきょく）: Introduces the eventual outcome; it is not necessarily a physical end point.
ja:〜ことになる: 〜ことになる: Can describe an arrangement or resulting situation; ことにする more directly describes making one's own decision.
ja:つまり: つまり: Clarifies an implication or summary; it should preserve the meaning of the preceding point.
ja:言い換えると: 言い換えると: Signals reformulation; a new contradictory claim is not simply a rewording.
ja:要するに: 要するに: Summarises the main point; abrupt intonation can sound dismissive.
ja:〜ということです: 〜ということです: Can restate an interpretation or report; it does not guarantee that the reported information is true.
ja:〜代わりに: 〜代わりに: Use the appropriate form before 代わりに, such as a dictionary verb or noun plus の.
ja:〜ではなく: 〜ではなく: Replaces one description or option with another; do not interpret it as accepting both.
ja:別の方法として: 別の方法として: Introduce a genuinely different method, not the same plan in different words.
ja:それとも: それとも: Used to offer a choice in a question; it is not the usual connector for a factual either-or statement.
ja:手を貸す: 手を貸す: Means offer practical help here, not literally lend a body part.
ja:手伝いましょうか: 手伝いましょうか: Offers the speaker's help; it does not ask the listener to do the helping.
ja:お願いがある: お願いがある: Introduces a request; the actual requested action still needs to follow.
ja:助かります: 助かります: Expresses that help is valuable; it does not claim the task has already been completed.
ja:なるほど: なるほど: Acknowledges understanding; with a formal superior, a different acknowledgement may be more appropriate.
ja:そういうことだったんですね: そういうことだったんですね: Marks a newly understood explanation; it does not necessarily mean you previously agreed with it.
ja:納得する: 納得する: Means accept something as convincing, which is stronger than merely hearing it.
ja:気づく: 気づく: Use に for the fact noticed; 気づく does not itself mean agree with that fact.
ja:比較検討する: 比較検討する: Means compare and examine before deciding; it does not necessarily announce a final choice.
ja:〜を踏まえて: 〜を踏まえて: Connects a decision to information taken into account; it does not mean the information proves the decision uniquely.
ja:一方で: 一方で: Introduces a contrasting aspect; both aspects may still be true.
ja:優先順位をつける: 優先順位をつける: Means rank competing needs; it does not mean every need can be handled at once.
ja:実行に移す: 実行に移す: Means start putting an idea into action, not merely continue discussing it.
ja:具体化する: 具体化する: Means make something concrete or operational; the implementation need not be complete yet.
ja:段階的に導入する: 段階的に導入する: Means introduce in stages, not launch everything at once.
ja:最後までやり遂げる: 最後までやり遂げる: Emphasises carrying through to completion; simply starting does not satisfy the expression.
ja:手に負えない: 手に負えない: Means beyond one's capacity to manage; it is not about physically using one's hands.
ja:手が回らない: 手が回らない: Means lack the time or resources to attend to everything; it is not literal inability to turn a hand.
ja:手が足りない: 手が足りない: Means too few people are available; it does not necessarily mean the existing staff lack skill.
ja:抱え込みすぎる: 抱え込みすぎる: Means take too much upon oneself; it often suggests sharing responsibilities rather than accepting even more.
ja:投げ出さない: 投げ出さない: Means do not abandon the effort; it does not deny that changing an unworkable approach can be sensible.
ja:粘り強く取り組む: 粘り強く取り組む: Describes persistent effort; the context still determines whether the approach is effective.
ja:立ち直る: 立ち直る: Means recover after a setback; it does not mean the setback never happened.
ja:試行錯誤を重ねる: 試行錯誤を重ねる: Means learn through repeated attempts and adjustments; it is not simply repeat the same mistake unchanged.
ja:〜と整合的だ: 〜と整合的だ: Means consistent with; compatibility does not rule out other explanations.
ja:〜を裏付ける: 〜を裏付ける: Means provide supporting evidence; the strength of that support depends on the evidence.
ja:〜を排除できない: 〜を排除できない: Means cannot exclude a possibility; it does not mean the possibility is established as true.
ja:断定するには不十分だ: 断定するには不十分だ: Limits certainty, not necessarily the usefulness of all available evidence.
ja:〜を条件として: 〜を条件として: Introduces a requirement; it does not say the requirement has already been met.
ja:〜を前提として: 〜を前提として: Identifies an assumption; do not confuse an assumed condition with an established fact.
ja:〜限りにおいて: 〜限りにおいて: Formally limits the scope in which a claim holds; it is not an unconditional generalisation.
ja:ただし: ただし: Introduces a restriction or exception to the previous statement; do not ignore it when summarising.
ja:改善の余地がある: 改善の余地がある: Signals that something can be improved; name the area rather than assuming complete failure.
ja:十分とは言い難い: 十分とは言い難い: A restrained negative judgment; it does not mean that no useful part exists.
ja:再検討が望まれる: 再検討が望まれる: Recommends reconsideration without naming an agent; it does not report that reconsideration has already occurred.
ja:やや楽観的だ: やや楽観的だ: Can tactfully question the realism of an estimate; tone determines how critical it sounds.
ja:口火を切る: 口火を切る: Means be the first to speak or act in a sequence; it is not a literal fire in this context.
ja:協議を開始する: 協議を開始する: Formal wording for beginning deliberation; it does not imply that agreement has already been reached.
ja:話を切り出す: 話を切り出す: Means bring up a topic, often a sensitive one; it does not mean interrupt every speaker.
ja:下地を作る: 下地を作る: Means prepare a foundation; the main result is not necessarily achieved yet.
